steps: Stand up straight with your feet hip-width apart. Hold a bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands about shoulder-width apart, and let it hang in front of your thighs.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your chest lifted.
Bend your elbows and curl the bar up toward your shoulders. Only your forearms should move.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't swing your body or lean back to lift the weight. If you need to, it's too heavy.
Keep your elbows still at your sides and don't let them drift forward.
Keep your wrists straight.

steps: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your eyes directly under the bar. Put both feet flat on the floor.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing your feet), with your hands about shoulder-width apart, closer than a normal bench press.
Lift the bar off the hooks and hold it straight above your chest with your arms straight.
Lower the bar slowly to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Press the bar back up in a straight line until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't put your hands closer than shoulder-width. A very narrow grip strains your wrists and elbows.
Use the rack's safety bars or have someone stand behind the bench, and start with light weight.
Keep your wrists straight and never bounce the bar off your chest.

steps: Lie on your back on a flat bench, holding a bar with an overhand grip (palms facing your feet), hands about shoulder-width apart. Hold it straight above your chest with your arms straight.
Keep your upper arms still and pointing straight up.
Bend only your elbows to slowly lower the bar toward your forehead, or just behind your head. Your elbows should stay pointing at the ceiling.
Stop when the bar is a couple of inches from your head, then straighten your arms to bring it back up.
watchFor: The bar is over your face, so control it carefully. Start light and use a spotter if you can.
Keep your elbows from flaring out to the sides.
If you feel pain in your elbows, use a lighter weight, or stop.

steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with your palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your chest lifted.
Bend your elbows and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders. You can curl both arms together or one at a time.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't swing your body or lean back to lift the weight.
Keep your elbows at your sides and don't let them drift forward.
Lower slowly. That's half the work.

steps: Set a bench so the back tilts back at a slight angle, about 45 degrees. Sit back on it with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down beside you, with your palms facing forward. You'll feel a stretch in the front of your arms.
Keeping your upper arms still, bend your elbows and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't let your elbows move forward as you curl.
Use lighter weights than you would for a standing curl because the stretch makes it harder.
Keep your back and head against the bench.

steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with your palms facing your body, as if you were holding a hammer.
Keep your elbows close to your sides.
Bend your elbows and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders, keeping your palms facing each other the whole time.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't swing or lean back to lift the weight.
Keep your wrists straight and your elbows tucked in.
Lower under control.

steps: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet flat on the floor and your legs wide apart. Hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Lean forward slightly and rest the back of that upper arm against the inside of your thigh, so your arm hangs straight down.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, turning your palm toward your shoulder as you lift.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arm is straight.
Finish all your reps, then switch arms.
watchFor: Keep your upper arm still against your thigh. Don't swing.
Use a light weight and go slowly.
Don't twist your body to lift the weight.

steps: Stand or sit up straight with your feet flat on the floor. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, cupping the inside of one end.
Lift it overhead with your arms straight, with the dumbbell above your head.
Keeping your upper arms close to your head and still, bend your elbows to slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Lower until you feel a stretch in the back of your arms, then straighten your arms to lift it back up.
watchFor: The weight moves close to your head, so hold it firmly and use a weight you can control.
Keep your elbows from flaring out to the sides.
Don't arch your back.

steps: Stand next to a bench and place one hand and the same-side knee on it. Hold a dumbbell in the other hand.
Keep your back flat and your upper arm tucked against your side, parallel to the floor, with your elbow bent at a right angle.
Straighten your arm backward until it's fully straight, keeping your upper arm still.
Squeeze the back of your arm for a moment, then bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell slowly.
Finish all your reps, then switch arms.
watchFor: Only your forearm should move. Don't swing the weight.
Use a light weight. A heavy weight makes you swing.
Keep your back flat and don't twist your body.

steps: Set a cable to the lowest position and attach a straight bar. Stand facing the machine, about a step back, holding the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up).
Stand up straight with your feet hip-width apart, elbows close to your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows still.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't lean back or swing your body to lift the weight.
Keep your elbows tucked in and your wrists straight.
Control the bar on the way down.

steps: Set a cable to the highest position and attach a straight bar or rope. Stand facing the machine, about a step back, with your feet hip-width apart.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down) and pull it down until your elbows are bent at a right angle, with your elbows tucked against your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Squeeze the back of your arms, then let the bar rise slowly until your forearms are just past level.
watchFor: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides. Don't let them drift forward.
Don't lean over the bar and use your body weight to push it down.
Control the bar on the way up.

steps: Set a cable to the highest position and attach a rope. Face away from the machine, take the rope in both hands, and step forward so there is tension in the cable.
Stand with one foot slightly in front, and lift the rope so your hands are behind your head with your elbows bent and pointing forward.
Keeping your upper arms still, straighten your arms out in front of you until they're fully straight.
Slowly bend your elbows to return the rope behind your head.
watchFor: Keep your elbows from flaring out to the sides.
Don't arch your lower back. Keep your stomach tight.
Use a weight you can control the whole way back.

steps: Sit at the machine and adjust the seat so your upper arms rest flat on the angled pad, with your armpits against the top.
Hold the handles with an underhand grip (palms facing up) and let your arms hang straight down against the pad.
Curl the handles up toward your shoulders, keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.
watchFor: Don't lower all the way to fully locked-out arms. That puts strain on your elbows.
Don't lift your body off the seat to move the weight.
Lower slowly under control.

steps: Sit at the machine and adjust the seat so the handles are by your sides. Put your feet on the footrests if there are any.
Take hold of the handles and sit up straight with your back against the pad.
Push the handles down until your arms are straight.
Pause, then let them rise slowly until your elbows are bent at a right angle.
watchFor: Keep your elbows close to your body and your shoulders down.
Don't lock your elbows hard at the bottom.
Don't let the weight stack slam.

steps: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench or chair with your hands on the edge beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Slide your hips off the edge and walk your feet forward, so that your arms support your weight. Keep your legs bent, or straighten them for a harder version.
Bend your elbows straight back and lower your body until your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Push through your hands to straighten your arms and lift yourself back up.
watchFor: Make sure the bench can't slide or tip.
Don't lower past level with the floor, and don't let your shoulders roll forward. That strains your shoulders.
Keep your back close to the bench and your elbows pointing straight back, not flaring out.

steps: Get on the floor on your hands and toes. Place your hands flat on the floor right under your chest, a few inches apart.
Step your feet back so your body forms one straight line from your head to your heels.
Tighten your stomach and buttocks.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows pointing straight back and close to your sides.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.
watchFor: If your wrists hurt, spread your hands a little wider.
Don't let your hips sag. If you can't keep a straight body, do them with your knees on the floor.
Keep your elbows from flaring out to the sides.

steps: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in one hand. Rest your forearm on your thigh, or on the bench, with your palm facing up and your wrist hanging over the edge.
Let the dumbbell roll down toward your fingertips, then close your fingers around it.
Curl your wrist upward, lifting the dumbbell as high as you can, keeping your forearm still.
Lower slowly, letting the dumbbell roll back down to your fingertips.
Finish all your reps, then switch arms.
watchFor: Use a light weight. Your wrists are small and can be injured by heavy weights.
Move slowly. Keep your forearm flat and still.
If your wrist hurts, stop and lower the weight.

steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt, which is a belt with a chain that lets a weight plate hang from your waist. You can also hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Grab the two parallel bars and lift yourself up so your arms are straight and you're holding your whole body weight plus the extra weight.
Keep your body upright, and let your elbows point straight back.
Slowly bend your elbows and lower yourself until your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Push through your hands to lift yourself back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Only add weight once you can do this same movement with just your own body weight, smoothly and with good control. Start with a small weight.
Don't go lower than level with the floor. Deeper dips put a lot of stress on the shoulders.
Don't swing. Stay smooth and stop if your shoulders or elbows hurt.
